submissions.title: HyperSync: Real-Time Pairwise Hackathon Matrix
submissions.tagline: Autonomous scoring engine with Glicko-2 pairwise duels and zero-config self-hosting.
submissions.description:
## The Problem
Traditional hackathon judging suffers from judge fatigue, uneven calibration between strict and generous reviewers, and tedious manual spreadsheets.

## Our Solution
HyperSync transforms judging into an ultra-fast, scientifically calibrated experience:
- **Pairwise Head-to-Head Duels**: Judges quickly pick between two randomized projects, driving robust Glicko-2 rating convergence in 50% less time.
- **Z-Score Normalization Engine**: Automatically removes individual judge skew.
- **Docker-First Architecture**: Runs in 15 seconds with `docker compose up -d`.
- **Live SSE Event Stream**: Real-time updates without polling.

submissions.title: Aegis: Intelligent Judge Assistant & Anti-Plagiarism Sentry
submissions.tagline: AI-assisted rubric scoring suggestions with deep AST code similarity detection.
submissions.description:
## What it Does
Aegis audits code commits across public hackathon repos, analyzes submission narratives with LLM rubric alignment, and synthesizes balanced judge feedback briefs.

## Key Features
- **Git AST Differential Analyzer**: Flags unoriginal or pre-existing code with precision.
- **Smart Rubric Assistant**: Suggests score ranges based on functional criteria.
- **Self-Hostable Local Models**: Compatible with Ollama & local Docker models.

submissions.title: NeuroFlow: Fluid Cyberpunk Submission Studio & Live Expo
submissions.tagline: Ultra-high polish participant submission studio with real-time video preview and Expo booth mode.
submissions.description:
## Experience Reimagined
Hackathons are about celebration and excitement. NeuroFlow brings a video-game tier UI to hackathon submissions with sound effects, dynamic markdown editor, and virtual showcase booths.

## Highlights
- **Interactive Expo Booths**: Participants customize their live project billboard.
- **Sub-100ms Markdown Engine**: Instant syntax highlighting and media embeds.
- **Accessibility First**: Full keyboard navigation & screen-reader compatibility.

submissions.title: OmniMesh: Zero-Dependency P2P Hackathon Node
submissions.tagline: Decentralized hackathon node running anywhere with multi-arch Docker and SQLite WAL replication.
submissions.description:
## Resilient Self-Hosting
Run your hackathon without AWS or cloud dependency. OmniMesh provides end-to-end encrypted peer syncing for multi-room offline hackathons.

## Features
- Single binary + multi-stage Docker build under 35MB.
- Automatic SQLite WAL backup and CSV export.
- Offline judge mode with background sync upon reconnect.

submissions.title: ZeroTrace: Anonymous Cryptographic Judging Ledger
submissions.tagline: Double-blind judging with homomorphic score aggregation preventing judge collusion.
submissions.description:
## Unbiased & Cryptographically Auditable
ZeroTrace guarantees complete anonymity for both submitters and judges until the embargo is lifted.
- **Double-Blind Submissions**: Identifiers stripped automatically during review.
- **Commit-Reveal Balloting**: Judges submit cryptographic hashes before final tally.
- **Instant Docker deployment** with zero external dependencies.

submissions.title: PromptMorph: Real-time Audio-Visual Hackathon Showcase
submissions.tagline: Turns project repos and slides into interactive 3D video pitches for instant judge comprehension.
submissions.description:
## Accelerate Judge Comprehension
Judges are swamped with dozens of projects. PromptMorph parses code repos and creates an interactive 90-second dynamic synthesis with architecture diagrams.

- **Auto-generated Architecture Charts**: Extracted directly from docker-compose and package manifests.
- **Interactive Pitch Mode**: Audio narration + live code snippets.

evaluations.feedback: Outstanding architecture. The Glicko-2 pairwise engine combined with Z-Score normalization solves real judge calibration problems. Clean Docker compose setup with instant startup.
Strong AST parser and code inspection engine. Impressive integration with Ollama for local self-hosted LLM execution.
Exceptional resilience and minimal binary footprint. Excellent offline-first synchronization.
Superb UI styling! The dark obsidian and neon violet themes look extremely professional. Pairwise voting duel modal is smooth and responsive.
World-class visual aesthetics and micro-interactions. The submission studio live preview feels like a AAA creative tool.
Good UI clarity, though the cryptographic commit-reveal flow could benefit from additional visual status indicators.
Top tier self-hosting execution. One single docker-compose file brings up everything with persistent data volumes and healthchecks.
Truly impressive 35MB multi-stage Alpine build. Perfect for edge hackathons with spotty venue WiFi.

faqs.question: What is Dogfood 2026?
faqs.answer: Dogfood 2026 is a 72-hour global hackathon where builders create the ultimate open-source, self-hostable hackathon submission and judging platform. The winning project will literally become the platform used for future global hackathons.

faqs.question: What are the self-hosting requirements?
faqs.answer: Your project must be easily runnable via Docker / Docker Compose in under 30 seconds with persistent data storage (e.g. SQLite WAL or PostgreSQL) and zero mandatory third-party vendor lock-in. Healthcheck endpoints (/health) are strongly recommended.

faqs.question: How does the Dual-Engine scoring matrix work?
faqs.answer: Scores are computed using two scientifically backed methods: 70% Z-Score Normalized Rubric Evaluations (which eliminates variance between harsh and lenient reviewers) and 30% Head-to-Head Pairwise Elo Duels (based on Glicko-2 rating convergence).

faqs.question: Can our team submit to multiple tracks?
faqs.answer: Every submission selects one Primary Track for the category prizes, but all projects are automatically eligible for the $20,000 Grand Prix and Community Choice Awards.

faqs.question: What must be included in our final submission?
faqs.answer: 1. A public GitHub/GitLab repository link with an open-source license. 2. Working Dockerfile or docker-compose.yml. 3. A 2-minute video pitch demonstration. 4. Clear README setup instructions.
